body.statement: Can the attainable Gaussian-tube calibration handle construct \(\widetilde C_N\) with \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}P_N\{\beta\in\widetilde C_N\}=1-\alpha\), a uniformly continuous reference quantile, and a certified approximation from above, simultaneously for \(\lambda_N=0\), bounded local amplitudes, diverging amplitudes, exponent endpoints, and nonconvergent allowed design sequences?
body.justification: This is the nonroutine open step separating conservative honesty from exact least-favorable coverage with attainable critical values.
body.gap: Andrews and Mikusheva establish generic conditional size control, but they do not analyze this curved cone, its diverging-amplitude tangent limits, or certified continuum optimization on changing spatial designs.
body.consumer: A positive answer yields less conservative reported intervals while preserving the uniform guarantee needed for the county-centroid application.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform anti-concentration and quantile-attainment theorem for \(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\) over bounded local amplitudes, \(|\lambda|\to\infty\), exponent endpoints, and nonconvergent allowed design sequences, together with a certified one-sided numerical approximation of the resulting attainable supremum quantile.
obligation.obstruction: Bounded-Lipschitz convergence alone does not control probabilities at a changing family of profile boundaries. The diverging-amplitude limits change from tangent planes in the exponent interior to one-sided tangent half-planes at the endpoints, and the frozen assumptions provide neither the required uniform anti-concentration modulus nor a computable representation of the nuisance compactum sufficient for interval certification.
obligation.attempted: Compactify the uniformly bounded \(C^1\) curves and positive-definite matrices; use Gaussian tube continuity for bounded \(\lambda\); rescale \(p-p_0\) by \(|\lambda|\) for tangent-plane and endpoint half-plane limits; and define the critical value as the supremum of attainable Gaussian quantiles. These steps establish the candidate limit families but do not prove a uniform continuity modulus across their junctions or certified continuum optimization from the stated primitives.
obligation.partial_result:
The already proved conservative construction gives, uniformly over all the listed amplitude and endpoint regimes,
\[
 \liminf_N\inf_{(P_N,\mathcal S_N)\in\mathcal M}P_N\{\beta\in C_N\}\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad \operatorname{diam}(C_N)\le C_\alpha N^{-1/2}.
\]
For each fixed \(N\), design, and attainable pair \((\lambda,p)\), the Gaussian statistic
\(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\) is explicit and its quantile is bounded above by \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\).  What is not supplied by the frozen assumptions is the uniform anti-concentration and compactified tangent-limit argument needed to replace this conservative critical value by the supremum of attainable quantiles while retaining equality of the lower coverage envelope.
